transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I'd like to get our pre-lock round-robin started so we can move toward final production approval. Let's go through each area: technical, rights, talent, and accessibility leads — please report your final operating requirements. I need to hear from all four before I can sign off on the production package.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical technical requirement from my completed RF survey. Wireless roaming camera links interfere with the theater's assistive-listening loop, so the gala must use three fixed wired cameras from the marked camera platforms. I filed the survey in the technical folder, but it's not on Mara's draft lock sheet yet. This means the current draft package's three-camera setup is fine, but they must be fixed wired cameras on the marked platforms — no wireless roaming.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a critical rights restriction to report. My signed performance license permits the gala broadcast but prohibits any video-on-demand release or later promotional clips. The recording must be marked broadcast-only. I received the countersigned license this morning and have not yet entered the restriction in the rights tracker, so the current draft package needs to be updated to reflect this. Specifically, the festival archive reuse provision in the current draft package conflicts with this license term and must be removed.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a critical talent requirement to report. I confirmed with the headliner's agent that the performer can soundcheck only at exactly 3:00 PM on Saturday, and the rider prohibits sponsor product placement anywhere on the performance stage. I have the agent's confirmation in email, but it is not in the production schedule. This means two things: first, the soundcheck must be scheduled for exactly 3:00 PM Saturday — no other time will work for the headliner. Second, the current draft package's sponsor product display on stage directly conflicts with the headliner's rider and must be removed from the stage area.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a critical accessibility requirement to report. My accessibility vendor confirmed that the live caption feed requires the captioner to work from Booth B, whose dedicated return feed is connected to the gala's caption encoder. The general plan's control-room location will not work for the caption feed. I documented the vendor confirmation in the accessibility file, but I have not yet added the booth assignment to the lock sheet. This means the lock sheet must be updated to assign the captioner to Booth B rather than the control-room location in the current draft plan.
